intent.goal: Keep the #382 mutual exclusion on evidence-run.py's ledger append while leaving no file beside the manifest, so a committed manifest leaves a clean tree and the next run's recorded wtree equals the committed tree.
intent.ruled_out: An unlink-after-close sidecar (a late joiner opens a fresh inode after the unlink and races the waiter that still holds the old one — the lost-record race returns); a stable out-of-tree lock under a temp dir keyed by the manifest path (litter moves rather than vanishing, tmp reapers can delete a held lock and silently split exclusion, and two spellings of one path need canonicalizing); an inode-identity re-check loop against rename-replacing writers (no writer in runtime/ or scripts/ replaces a manifest by rename — grep for os.replace/rename is empty — and egress.py locks its ledger inode the same way without one); manifest schema, verify.py, .gitignore, and cleaning up pre-fix *.lock files (out of scope).
intent.why: The manifest is already the one file every cooperating writer opens, and append_record rewrites it in place, so its own inode is a lock with no extra file and no lifetime to manage. It is the idiom egress.py already uses for its ledger. The only behaviour change is that a zero-length manifest is read as the not-yet-written one, which the O_CREAT open itself produces.

commands_note: All three records were written by runtime/scripts/evidence-run.py (the fixed wrapper) on the clean tree of head_sha 75c0c91 (wtree 0e6aa479 == head_tree). The manifest was moved aside between runs so each run started on that clean tree with no manifest present; the records are concatenated here byte-for-byte as the recorder wrote them. The first record is the coordinator-named NC-COMMAND verbatim.

Rollout window: a pre-fix wrapper (locking <manifest>.lock) and a fixed wrapper (locking the manifest) do not exclude each other if they append to one manifest concurrently; and <manifest>.lock files left by pre-fix runs are not removed (pre-lock history is out of scope).
The in-place truncate+write is not atomic for LOCK-FREE readers (verify.py reads without the lock); unchanged from base, where write_text also truncated in place.
